meta.title: Scope — where a task's `scope` field comes from
meta.frame: The task-create skill's '## Scope' section, as a graph instead of prose. Answers: where does scope come from, what does NOT influence it, what goes wrong, and what to do about it. Not an implementation trace of taskfw/scope.py -- see that file's docstring for the actual code path.

relation_types.determines: the left node is what actually decides the right node's value
relation_types.does_not_affect: a plausible-looking influence that turns out to do nothing here
relation_types.causes: left node's behavior produces right node as a consequence
relation_types.fixes: left node is the corrective action for the right node's problem

nodes.label: Directory the taskfw MCP server was launched in
nodes.definition: Fixed once, at session start. This is the actual source of scope -- long-lived, not touched again for the rest of the session.

nodes.label: Agent running `cd` in a shell tool
Harness's reported "current working directory"
nodes.definition: Can change mid-conversation (e.g. after a shell cd). Looks like it should matter. Doesn't.

nodes.label: task.scope (git:<host>/<path> / path:<abs> / hint:<text>)
nodes.definition: Set once at tasks__create time from server_launch_dir's git remote (or its path, if no remote).

nodes.label: Session touches a different repo than it started in
Task filed under the wrong project
nodes.definition: Nothing errors. The task just sits under a scope that doesn't match `files`, until a listing looks off.

nodes.label: Compare returned `scope` against the real repo of `files`
tasks__update(task_id, scope="git:<host>/<path>")
nodes.definition: Use the target repo's actual git remote, not a guessed name.
